name: Lamium

project_scope.lesson_scope: Two canonical Lamium encounter species now installed with physical exact-taxon licensed images: henbit L. amplexicaule and purple deadnettle L. purpureum. Glechoma is a DIFFERENT genus and comparison-only. Both Lamium treated as introduced Texas species, excluded from native plant counts.
project_scope.science_status: Both Lamium species introduced (L. purpureum POWO confirmed introduced Texas); no target-county native claims or official invasive status asserted.

look_here_first: TWO-WAY CREW KEY: UPPER LEAVES first. HENBIT L. amplexicaule has round, deeply scalloped sessile green COLLARS surrounding square stem; PURPLE DEADNETTLE L. purpureum has more pointed often-purple crowded top leaves with small PETIOLES (lift a top leaf to see the hidden stalk). Both have opposite leaves and purple two-lipped flowers. Ground ivy Glechoma is a perennial creeper with stalked leaves.
shared_traits: Lamiaceae mint family: most forms have opposite leaves and four-sided stems, flowers with five fused corolla lobes in two lips, and often four nutlets in persistent green calyx.
Lamium species commonly have pinkish/purple tubular two-lipped flowers in false whorls (verticillasters) at leaf nodes.
Leaves often toothed/scalloped; do not assume all Lamium species have sessile/clasping upper leaves—that distinguishes henbit among common look-alikes.
Do not assume all mint-family plants smell minty; scent is variable and not useful alone for henbit.

genus_diagnostics.family_connection: Lamiaceae recognition: opposite leaves, four-angled stem and bilabiate fused corolla; fruit typically four nutlets, but individual characters not absolute across the family.
genus_diagnostics.genus_vs_family: Lamium has a long tubular corolla with a hood-like upper lip, lower lip with lobes and markings, opposite scalloped leaves and dense flower whorls around the upper nodes. Contrast creeping ground ivy Glechoma and other mints.
high_value_parts: Upper leaf attachment (petiole vs sessile clasp)
Long flower tube and distinct hood/lower lip
Whole growth form (winter annual versus perennial creeping)
genus_diagnostics.cross_genus_warning: Ground ivy Glechoma hederacea is a different genus; it may be encountered as a look-alike but NOT a canonical Lamium record in this project.

visual_comparison.title: Lamium field identification — henbit versus purple deadnettle
visual_comparison.subtitle: Both canonical Lamium cards now represented with 9 real photographic panels and 29 visible-anatomy arrows, including freshly checked purple deadnettle flower/lip/calyx and upper purple cap. Source-licensed, accurate compare-only labels. The petiole insertion and nutlets remain photographic gaps.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: HENBIT = rounded scalloped SESSILE green upper collar. PURPLE DEADNETTLE = pointed often purple upper CAP with SHORT PETIOLES (verify in field). Both are introduced; purple color alone is not diagnosis.

items.label: 1 · HENBIT HABIT — long lower petioles to sessile flower tiers
items.creator: Harry Rose
items.caption: Actual source photograph of flowering henbit held in hand. LOOSELY UPRIGHT SHOOT, a tier of rounded scalloped UPPER LEAVES surrounding the stem directly, and smaller LOWER ROUND LEAVES on long thin PETIOLES. The shoot's four-angled stem cannot be confirmed from this picture, even though it is a normal family character.
items.why_it_matters: The developmental difference between lower stalked and upper stalkless leaf pairs is the highest-value field clue.
items.photo_status: PHYSICALLY INSTALLED original Harry Rose CC BY 2.0, image pixels inspected; arrows only to visible whorls, stalk, leaf and flower; phone QA pending.

items.label: 2 · HENBIT FLOWER — upper hood, long tube, lower lip
items.creator: Harry Rose
items.caption: Actual flowers show a distinctly LONG PURPLE TUBE, a hairy upright UPPER LIP or HOOD, and small contrasting LOWER LIP lobes; flowers arise in groups just above a ring of shallowly lobed green leaves. The central bract/calyx structure is cluttered; individual nutlets are not visible.
items.why_it_matters: Separates a two-lipped mint-family corolla from unrelated tiny purple lawn flowers; a purple petal alone is never genus proof.
items.photo_status: PHYSICALLY INSTALLED original Harry Rose CC BY 2.0, anatomical targets inspected from bytes; no false fruit or stigma arrow; phone QA pending.

items.label: 3 · HENBIT CLOSE FLOWER AND WHORLS — verified additional source
items.creator: Tamberly Conway
items.caption: A Tennessee-source henbit has MANY lavender hooded tubular flowers arising from two upper whorls of ROUND SCALLOPED LEAVES, with several DARK MAGENTA CLOSED BUDS below. This shows the organ's POSITION at a stem node; the complete 360° clasping junction is partly obscured by leaves.
items.why_it_matters: Strong close identification of henbit's flowering whorls and scalloped opposite leaves; cannot be counted as a Texas native plant record.
items.photo_status: EXTERNAL VERIFIED CC BY 4.0, Tamberly Conway, iNaturalist 130042537 Commons source; inspected thumbnail actual pixels, 3 anatomy-target arrows, no photo bytes installed.

items.label: 4 · HENBIT LOWER FLOWERING TIER — sessile whorl
items.creator: TeunSpaans
items.caption: A close source-confirmed henbit plant shows rounded-to-fan-shaped green upper leaves around the ascending stem and several hooded pink flowers at the upper node. Another round scalloped whorl appears LOWER on the same flowering stem. A photo from the Netherlands; not local Texas provenance.
items.why_it_matters: At upper nodes, henbit leaves can appear like a collar, rather than separate dangling petioles as in purple deadnettle.
items.photo_status: EXTERNAL VERIFIED CC BY-SA 3.0 TeunSpaans, image preview reviewed, all 3 arrow targets visibly in frame. Original unaltered; phone QA pending.

items.label: 5 · LOOK-ALIKE ONLY — Purple deadnettle (NOT HENBIT)
items.creator: Arthur Badel
items.caption: NOT HENBIT: this is Lamium purpureum, purple deadnettle. Above the greener lower leaves is a DENSE CAP OF PURPLISH, MORE TRIANGULAR/POINTED UPPER LEAVES; the purple flowers are partly tucked below. Upper leaves usually keep short petioles, though the actual stalks are not fully resolved in this photo.
items.why_it_matters: Visually memorable confusion species. For certainty, trace the leaf base: purple deadnettle is often STALKED above, henbit is SESSILE/CLASPING above. Purple tint alone is not a dependable universal character.
items.photo_status: Physically installed exact L. purpureum photograph in new canonical species, maintained author/license and preverified arrows.

items.label: 6 · LOOK-ALIKE ONLY — Ground ivy (NOT HENBIT)
items.creator: NY State IPM Program at Cornell University
items.caption: NOT HENBIT AND NOT Lamium: this is creeping ground ivy, Glechoma hederacea, with green scalloped leaves and broader PURPLE TWO-LIPPED FLOWERS. Leaves are PETIOLATE at flowering nodes; the true runner habit must be confirmed by following the stem beyond this cropped view.
items.why_it_matters: Ground ivy is perennial and typically creeps/rooting at nodes, unlike the cool-season annual henbit; check leaf stalks and growth habit together.
items.photo_status: COMPARE-ONLY, DIFFERENT GENUS. Cornell NY State IPM CC BY 2.0 license verified; no arrow for a runner not actually shown.

items.label: PURPLE DEADNETTLE — second independently sourced whole plant
items.creator: Sarah Stierch
items.caption: Several genuine purple deadnettle flowering shoots with purple-tinged pointed upper leaf caps, pink flowers between them, and rounder green, coarse-scalloped lower leaves. Nearby clover and grasses are OTHER vegetation. Use overall habit, not a false inferred upper petiole.
items.why_it_matters: Independent exact-species recognition photo, not an unlabeled generic mint-family stand-in.
items.photo_status: 3 pixels-verified real plant-part annotations; no petiole claim; source original CC0 photograph. Mobile QA pending.

items.label: PURPLE DEADNETTLE — new licensed real flower anatomy source
items.creator: Alexander Abair
items.image_role: Flowering L. purpureum original France source; image depicts purple corolla with calyx, site-verified taxon source.
items.caption: Extreme close-up of a purple deadnettle corolla: hairy pale LAVENDER HOOD, lower lip with purple markings, visibly hairy green calyx with long teeth under the corolla, and an adjacent scalloped leaf blade. These are real visible features; the image does NOT show mature nutlets or the crucial upper leaf petiole.
items.why_it_matters: Independent close flower view will allow hood, lower lip, and calyx cues to be highlighted after image-specific arrow review.
items.photo_status: 4 real anatomical pixel targets inspected on the source-exact physical licensed flower macro; no invented petiole/seed arrow. Mobile overlay QA remains pending.

items.label: PURPLE DEADNETTLE — new licensed real flower anatomy source
items.creator: MurielBendel
items.image_role: Additional flower/branch macro of L. purpureum from Switzerland, distinct source; flower parts pending arrow review.
items.caption: Flowering true L. purpureum with crowding of dark pointed upper leaves, partly hooded pink two-lipped flowers, and a broad greenish crenate leaf below. Photograph includes other vegetation; do not attribute all grasses or nearby round leaves to the purple deadnettle. Upper petiole insertion remains hidden.

part_examples.title: 1 · Lower leaf: petiole
part_examples.look_for: A thin, long stalk connects a rounded scalloped lower blade to the stem.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Proves leaf development transition within henbit; don't assume all leaves are sessile.

part_examples.title: 2 · Upper leaf: sessile collar
part_examples.look_for: A green leaf tier encircling a flowering node with no evident long petioles.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Key henbit versus purple deadnettle split.

part_examples.title: 3 · Flower: two-lipped hood
part_examples.look_for: Narrow purple corolla tube, arched hairy upper lip, speckled lower lip above leafy cup.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Core Lamium flower structure, not the only species clue.

part_examples.title: 4 · NEED PHOTO: square stem cross-section
part_examples.look_for: Four ridges on a measured genuine henbit stem cross section.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Family confirmation; NOT proof from an unresolvable front view.

part_examples.title: 5 · NEED PHOTO: ripe fruit/nutlets
part_examples.look_for: Dry five-toothed calyx and four separated brown nutlets at 1-mm ruler scale.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Completes seed stage rather than guessing fruit inside flower photograph.

comparison_cards.title: Henbit vs purple deadnettle (both Lamium)
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Trace the UPPER leaf to its stem junction, not merely the purple flower. Henbit upper leaves form rounded scalloped stalkless COLLARS; L. purpureum usually has triangular/pointed purple or green leaves on SHORT PETIOLES.

field_matrix.purple_deadnettle: Upper leaf still has short PETIOLE, not a continuous collar

field_matrix.henbit: Round to kidney/fan-shaped with blunt scallops

field_matrix.purple_deadnettle: Also stalked; basal leaves often broader

field_matrix.henbit: Pink purple two-lipped tubes, long thin tube

comparison_cards.caution: Both Lamium cards are installed. The henbit green upper collars and purple deadnettle purple leaf cap/flower anatomy are photographed, but the short upper petiole insertion on L. purpureum remains hidden. Do not manufacture a petiole arrow; follow a real node in the field.

comparison_cards.title: Henbit vs ground ivy (Lamium vs Glechoma)
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Check whether the plant is an annual with upper clasping leaf collars (henbit), or a creeping long-lived stolon-former with STALKED leaves all the way to flowers (ground ivy).

field_matrix.ground_ivy: Creeping perennial, runners root at nodes

field_matrix.henbit: Rounded SESSILE upper collars clasp stem
field_matrix.ground_ivy: Rounded, scalloped but PETIOLATE, even near flowers

field_matrix.henbit: Long narrow pink-purple hooded tubes in clustered upper-node whorls
field_matrix.ground_ivy: Broader blue-purple flowers in leaf axils

comparison_cards.caution: Glechoma hederacea is a DIFFERENT GENUS, and this comparison does not claim it's a locally certified native or installed Lamium species.

lookalike_warnings: Purple deadnettle L. purpureum: true Lamium congener but now installed as an introduced exact-species learner card; upper leaves remain stalked and tend to form purple pointed caps.
Ground ivy Glechoma hederacea: creeping perennial in separate genus, never accidentally label as a Lamium or henbit photo.
Leaf attachment changes along henbit stem: lower leaves have petioles, flowering upper leaves are sessile. Do not teach 'henbit has only stalkless leaves'.
Four-sided stems, opposite leaves, two-lipped flowers and nectar are FAMILY-/GUILD-level traits, not enough to force species ID.
Henbit is introduced in Texas in project rules; no native restoration recommendation or automatic invasive status.

comparison_matrix.henbit: Round upper leaves sessile and clasp stem
comparison_matrix.purple_deadnettle: Upper leaves petiolate and more triangular
Pink tubes under pointed leaf cap
